title: Topic 11 · Status Games vs. Wealth Creation · Chunks
source: Modern Wisdom · Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant · youtu.be/KyfUysrNaco

items.s: Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
There’s a real draw of being swayed by social approval, but how should people learn to get less distracted by status games in that way?

items.c: there was no such thing as wealth
items.s: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.
You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.
So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.

items.zh: 我们在进化上天生如此
items.s: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.

items.c: it's not gonna fall on your lap
items.zh: 它不会自己掉到你怀里
items.s: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting,

items.c: almost no way out of that
items.s: A few hundred years ago you were born a serf, you were gonna die a serf, there was almost no way out of that.
A lot of people do that, as you said.
That’s a good observation, I hadn’t thought that through, but you’re right.

items.c: trajectory is more important than position
items.s: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.
